messages:
julia: heads-up — onboarding session: Go sample app using Generator.Stream inside an HTTP handler sometimes never returns after an auth refresh. observed in macOS dev laptops and CI. stack snippet below, happens ~1/20 runs :confused:

julia: stack (abridged):
```
net/http: handler started
runtime: goroutine 512 locked to thread
...
generator.Stream handshake -> waiting on token refresh
http handler waiting on Stream loop to finish
```

julia: repro: hit the sample with `wrk -c 20 -d 30s` while forcing the auth token to expire every 2s (local auth proxy). sometimes handler goroutines pile up.

kevin: can you paste the minimal handler you use? curious if it's streaming inside request goroutine or spawning worker goroutine.

julia: sure — simplified handler:```go
func StreamHandler(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
  ctx := r.Context()
  gen := client.Generator("gpt-lite")
  stream, err := gen.Stream(ctx, prompt)
  if err != nil { http.Error(w, err.Error(), 500); return }
  for chunk := range stream.Chunks() { fmt.Fprint(w, chunk.Text) }
}
```

kevin: aha. so the Stream handshake does an auth check and may trigger a refresh which does network I/O. if refresh blocks and the client cancels, the generator goroutine can get stuck waiting on the handshake while the HTTP server is blocked on writing the response.

sam: this smells like two problems: (1) the handshake uses the request ctx (so it cancels), (2) token refresher may be serialized and not cancel-safe. short-term: spawn the generator handshake on a child ctx with a small timeout or use non-cancelable background for the handshake stage. e.g.:
```go
hsCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 2*time.Second)
defer cancel()
stream, err := gen.Stream(hsCtx, prompt)
```
That keeps the HTTP ctx free to control the stream lifetime.

julia: tried that, it reduces hangs but then sometimes you get handshake succeed and subsequent Refresh() fails mid-stream and we still leak a goroutine.

kevin: thinking: SDK ergonomics should be clearer — generator.Stream(ctx, ...) currently uses ctx for both handshake and for ongoing stream. maybe we expose StreamWithHandshake(ctx, handshakeCtx, opts) or at least doc the race.

ci-bot: test generator/stream-onboarding flaky_test.go: FAIL (timeout) — reproducing locally with wrk pattern provided by julia (run id: 98f3).

sam: filing a tiny SDK proposal: 1) separate handshake context, 2) add Stream.Close() that force-drains and cancels internal goroutines, 3) doc a recommended pattern for HTTP handlers. will sketch in PR.

julia: +1 on all three. the surprising part for new devs is that normal `defer stream.Close()` in handler doesn't always finish because Close waits for handshake to resolve.

kevin: I'll take the API PR to propose `StartStream(ctx, handshakeCtx, opts)` and add a note in the Go quickstart about not using r.Context() directly for handshake.

sam: also adding a CI test that rotates tokens under load to prevent regressions.

julia: thanks — I'll open the GH issue and attach the wrk script and auth-proxy. assigning to @kevin for API design. :party-parrot:

kevin: thanks. if anyone else hit similar, drop short repro here (OS, go version, whether using SDK v0.9.x or v0.10.x).
